newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on hedge pressure.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on hedge pressure.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled just above their intraday lows on hedge selling tied to increased country movement, traders said.

One trader described Thursday's session as "a correction to yesterday's correction," explaining that some players were evening up their positions and clearing some of their longs ahead of Friday's USDA crop report, which will include the government's latest estimate of 1997 U.S. HRW wheat output.
Traders said wheat faltered further on spillover pressure from corn and beans, which were lower on forecasts for good crop growing weather.
A lack of fund-buying also helped wheat prices weaken.

"We missed the fund-buying component, and even though we saw some nice commercial buying today, it was not enough to offset the hedge pressure (from increased country movement)," another KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat settled two to 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 2-3/4 cents at $3.30-3/4. September lost 5-1/4 cents to close at $3.34-1/4.
Volumes were lighter than those seen in recent days. The KCBT estimated Thursday's wheat futures volume at 52.425 million bushels, down from 73.79 million Wednesday.

Traders said CIS bought 3.2 million Sept and Term Commodities bought two million Dec bushels. Farmers Commodities sold two million Sept. E. D. & F. Man International, Continental Grain, Term Commodities and Wolcott Lincoln each sold at least one million Sept bushels.
